sentences.text: 2. Bistari Pradhan  Mr. S. Bahadur, Advocate  -versus-  State of Odisha ....
Mr. M.K. Mohanty, ASC  CORAM: JUSTICE V. NARASINGH

Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners and learned counsel for the State.
2.

The Petitioners are seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with G.R. Case No.989 of 2009 pending on the file of learned S.D.J.M., Jharsuguda arising out of Jharsuguda P.S. Case No.290 of 2009 for commission of offences punishable under Sections 467/468/471/474/420/34 of IPC.
3. Admittedly the Petitioners were before this Court in BLAPL Nos.11843 & 11816 of 2009 respectively.

4. It is submitted that in terms of the order passed by this Court, since charge sheet was filed,
summons were issued in 2025 and because of supervening circumstances, since the Petitioners could not appear in pursuance to such summons, they are apprehending arrest.
5. Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for pre-arrest bail.

6. Taking into account the nature of allegations and the earlier order passed, it is directed that the Petitioners shall surrender on or before 19.01.2026 before the the learned Court in seisin and on such surrendering, they shall be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin on such terms as deemed just and proper.

8. In the event the Petitioners do not surrender on the date fixed, it shall be open for the Investigating Agency to take action against them in accordance with law.
9. The ABLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
